Each adapter version: about 21 MB. Data needed before each layer is useful: | Layer | Minimum data | | --- | --- | | 1–2 Rules and handover | 1 session; rules need a fact seen in 2+ sessions or in config | | 3 Your own examples | About 20 committed tasks in the project | | 4 Formatter hook | The repo's existing config; no history needed | | 5 LoRA | At least 3 sessions and about 500 accepted examples; 30+ bench tasks before the gate can judge it | Privacy: everything stays under ~/.footprint and the repo. No data leaves the machine; vault sync of training data is off unless you opt in. ## 9. Intelligence layer Pick the model last, behind a small registry, so memory and the pipeline never depend on it. The hardware decides which models are even possible. Model registry (one small file, no framework): ```json {"active": "qwen2.5-coder-1.5b", "models": { "qwen2.5-coder-1.5b": {"mlx": "mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct-4bit", "min_ram_gb": 8, "trainable": true} }} ``` footprint model use switches the active model, and its adapter if one exists for that model. Memory is unchanged. Cloud models (Big Pickle, GLM, Gemini) get memory but no adapter. What fits in memory (approximate: weights only, about 2 bytes per parameter at bf16 and about 0.55 at 4-bit): | Model size | bf16 weights | 4-bit weights | 8 GB M1: run | 8 GB M1: train LoRA | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1.5B | \~3 GB | \~0.9 GB | Yes | Yes | | 3–4B | \~7 GB | \~2 GB | 4-bit only | 4-bit, tight | | 9B | \~18 GB | \~5 GB | 4-bit, very tight | No | | 26–31B | \~55–62 GB | \~15–17 GB | No | No | Only about 5–6 GB of the 8 GB is usable after macOS. So on this machine, quantisation is not optional above about 2B. "Higher precision first" needs 32 GB or more. Candidates from the proposal (names, sizes and licences still to verify before use): - Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B — current baseline, fits today. - Qwen3.5 9B and 27B — 9B is the realistic upgrade on a 16–32 GB machine. - Gemma 4 — check whether a 12B exists; the 26B A4B mixture-of-experts still needs all weights in memory. - NVIDIA Nemotron — check which coding checkpoint and its licence. Decide with the bench, not with leaderboards: same tasks, same memory, each model. ## 10. Evaluation Nothing is called an improvement until the bench shows it. The bench already exists; it needs more tasks and personalisation metrics. Experiments (same tasks, same repo state, same tools): | Run | Memory | LoRA | Answers | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | off | off | Baseline | | B | on | off | What memory adds | | C | off | on | What LoRA adds | | D | on | on | Combined | Metrics: | Group | Metric | How measured | | --- | --- | --- | | Coding | Task pass rate | Bench: the original check passes and at least one file changed | | Personalisation | Style match | Lint and format errors of the model's diff against the repo's own config | | Personalisation | Closeness to your accepted change | Edit distance to the diff you actually committed | | Personalisation | Correction rate in real use | Corrective follow-up prompts per task, read from logs (labeller from section 5) | | Memory | Retrieval hit rate | Was the relevant past task in the top 3? Needs a small labelled set | | System | Latency, peak RAM, training time | Logged per run | Approval gate for a new adapter: - [ ] Validation loss lower than the active adapter on the session-split test set - [ ] Bench pass rate not lower than the active adapter - [ ] Style match not worse - [ ] At least 30 bench tasks, so the numbers mean something Data rules: the newest sessions are the test set and are never trained on. Bench tasks are held out from memory and training (already true). ## 11. Roadmap Five phases in strict order; each starts only when the previous gate passes. Phase 1 is small and removes the privacy risk, so it comes first. ```mermaid flowchart TD P1["1. Data hygiene (start here)
Redact training data; split by session
Keep data local; archive transcripts"] --> G1{{"Gate: 0 secret hits; archive captures every new session"}} G1 --> P2["2. Labeller and bench
Accept/reject labels from chat and git
Grow the bench to 30+ tasks; style and correction metrics"] P2 --> G2{{"Gate: labels spot-checked on 50 tasks; bench has 30+ tasks"}} G2 --> P3["3. Memory facts
Profile from repo config and git; facts from corrections
Merge, supersede, inject under a budget"] P3 --> G3{{"Gate: experiment B (memory) beats A"}} G3 --> P4["4. LoRA v2
Native chat and tool format; accepted turns + your commits
Versioned adapters, rollback, background training"] P4 --> G4{{"Gate: C or D beats B; adapter passes approval checks"}} G4 --> P5["5. Model choice
Registry and switching; hardware decision first
Compare on the same bench and memory"] P5 --> G5{{"Gate: the bench picks the default model"}} style P1 fill:#e7f1fb,stroke:#2b6cb0,stroke-width:2px ``` Phase 2 is the hardest: git-based labels (commits, reverts, your own code) are the most reliable signal and the most work. If phase 3 gives most of the gain, phase 4 can wait. These decide scope; building before answering them risks rework. **Done on `main` (all changes since the last commit are uncommitted):**
- **1. Session handover** — committed.
- **2. Task recall (keyword search)** — committed.
- **3. User profile** — built this session; keyword-based.
- **4. Project memory** — built this session; keyword-based.
- **5. Semantic search** (embeddings through Ollama) — built this session.

**Plan's memory build order:**

| # | Step | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Archive sessions | ❌ Not built. No `~/.footprint/archive/`, and `cleanupPeriodDays` isn't set, so Claude Code is still deleting transcripts after about 30 days. |
| 2 | Classifier and labels | ⚠️ Corrections only, on the prototype branch `worktree-distill-pipeline` (commit `27548a5`), not merged. Questions, pastes and acknowledgements aren't classified yet. |
| 3 | Profile reader (lockfile, formatter, test command, commit style) | ❌ Today's profile reads only chat and a few marker files, not the repo config or git. |
| 4 | Rules store (`rules.json`: extract, merge, supersede, score) | ⚠️ Partly on the prototype branch: `footprint facts` writes v1 records and injects only ones seen 2+ times. No merging, superseding or scoring. |
| 5 | Inject within the token budget | ✅ Done for profile and project memory, using a character cap rather than tokens. |
| 6 | `footprint memory list / forget` | ❌ Not built. |

def facts(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Structured memory (schema v1): standing preferences the user stated in their own prompts.
    Derived from the task index on demand, so nothing is stored twice or goes stale.
    Same word-set across sessions = one record with more evidence; newest wording wins;
    seen in 2+ projects = user scope, else project scope. cwd filters to user + that project."""
    recs = {}
    for t in tasks:
        for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", t["prompt"]):
            s = s.strip(" -*>\t")
            if not (12 <= len(s) <= 200 and PREF.search(s)) or s.startswith(("<", "{", '"')) \
                    or s.endswith("?") or '":' in s or re.search(r"never ?mind", s, re.I):
                continue
            key = " ".join(sorted(set(_words(s))))
            if not key:
                continue
            r = recs.setdefault(key, {"kind": "correction" if is_correction(t["prompt"]) else "preference",
                                      "text": s, "projects": set(), "evidence": [],
                                      "first": t["t"], "last": t["t"]})
            r["projects"].add(t["cwd"] or "?")
            r["evidence"].append(t["id"])
            r["first"] = min(r["first"], t["t"])
            if t["t"] >= r["last"]:
                r["text"], r["last"] = s, t["t"]
    here = os.path.abspath(cwd) if cwd else None
    day = lambda ts: datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).date().isoformat()
    out = []
    for key, r in recs.items():
        n, projs = len(r["evidence"]), sorted(r["projects"])
        scope = "user" if len(projs) > 1 else f"project:{projs[0]}"
        if here and scope not in ("user", f"project:{here}"):
            continue
        out.append({"id": "f_" + hashlib.sha1(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], "schema": 1, "kind": r["kind"],
                    "scope": scope, "text": r["text"], "count": n,
                    "confidence": round(min(0.95, 0.5 + 0.15 * (n - 1)), 2),  # ponytail: evidence-count prior
                    "evidence": r["evidence"][-5:], "first_seen": day(r["first"]), "last_seen": day(r["last"]),
                    "_last": r["last"]})
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["count"], r.pop("_last")), reverse=True)
    return out


def render_facts(recs, cap=1200):
    recs = [r for r in recs if r["count"] >= FACT_MIN][:12]
    if not recs:
        return ""
    lines = ["# Standing preferences (footprint memory — stated by this user in past sessions; "
             "follow unless told otherwise)"]
    lines += [f"- {r['text']}" + (f" (x{r['count']})" if r["count"] > 1 else "") for r in recs]
    return "\n".join(lines)[:cap]

Steps 1–3 are done: three commits on the new branch `feat/memory-layers`, all tests and self-checks passing. Nothing is pushed, and `main` hasn't moved.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `77d7293` | Last session's memory work: profile, project memory, semantic search |
| `782458d` | Merge of the prototype branch (`worktree-distill-pipeline`) |
| `1ebe250` | Session archive and longer transcript retention |

**Merge:**
- There were conflicts in `memory.py` and `cli.py`. I resolved them so the prototype's evidence-based `facts` is now the only source of standing preferences: a preference is injected only after it shows up in 2 or more tasks. I deleted my keyword-based preference finder.
- `profile` now covers only habits and project memory.
- Session start builds the memory index once and prints, in order: preferences, then profile, then the handover.
- On your history, no preference has shown up twice yet, so that block is empty for now.

**Archive:**
- Every session idle for 30 minutes or more gets a redacted copy in `~/.footprint/archive/`.
- Memory reads the copy once Claude Code deletes the original.
- First run copied 99 MB in 8s. After that it takes about 0.15s per prompt.
- A scan of the archive for token-like secrets found none.

**Retention:**
- Your `~/.claude/settings.json` now has `cleanupPeriodDays: 3650`, so Claude Code keeps transcripts for 10 years.
- `context install` sets the same value for other users, but only if they haven't chosen one.

Two gaps:
- Training data (`footprint collect`) doesn't read the archive yet, only memory does.
- OpenCode sessions aren't archived. Its database isn't cleaned up the way Claude Code transcripts are, so I left it.

Your edit to `alternateApproach.md` is still uncommitted and untouched.

    """Session-start block: who you are as a developer + what this project is. '' when nothing learned."""
    here = [t for t in tasks if cwd and t["cwd"] and os.path.abspath(t["cwd"]) == os.path.abspath(cwd)]
    out = []  # standing preferences come from facts() (evidence-based), not from here
    tools = Counter(h for t in tasks for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(8)
    exts = Counter(os.path.splitext(f)[1] for t in tasks for f in t["files"] if os.path.splitext(f)[1]).most_common(6)
    habits = []
    if tools:
        habits.append("tools you run: " + ", ".join(k for k, _ in tools))

        if hot:
            proj.append("Most-edited files: " + ", ".join(f for f, _ in hot))
        tools = Counter(h for t in here for c in t["cmds"] for h in _heads(c)).most_common(6)

        out.append("\n".join(proj))

def facts(tasks, cwd=None):
    """Structured memory (schema v1): standing preferences the user stated in their own prompts.
    Derived from the task index on demand, so nothing is stored twice or goes stale.
    Same word-set across sessions = one record with more evidence; newest wording wins;
    seen in 2+ projects = user scope, else project scope. cwd filters to user + that project."""
    recs = {}
    for t in tasks:
        for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", t["prompt"]):
            s = s.strip(" -*>\t")
            if not (12 <= len(s) <= 200 and PREF.search(s)) or s.startswith(("<", "{", '"')) \
                    or s.endswith("?") or '":' in s or re.search(r"never ?mind", s, re.I):
                continue
            key = " ".join(sorted(set(_words(s))))
            if not key:
                continue
            r = recs.setdefault(key, {"kind": "correction" if is_correction(t["prompt"]) else "preference",
                                      "text": s, "projects": set(), "evidence": [],
                                      "first": t["t"], "last": t["t"]})
            r["projects"].add(t["cwd"] or "?")
            r["evidence"].append(t["id"])
            r["first"] = min(r["first"], t["t"])
            if t["t"] >= r["last"]:
                r["text"], r["last"] = s, t["t"]
    here = os.path.abspath(cwd) if cwd else None
    day = lambda ts: datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).date().isoformat()
    out = []
    for key, r in recs.items():
        n, projs = len(r["evidence"]), sorted(r["projects"])
        scope = "user" if len(projs) > 1 else f"project:{projs[0]}"
        if here and scope not in ("user", f"project:{here}"):
            continue
        out.append({"id": "f_" + hashlib.sha1(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], "schema": 1, "kind": r["kind"],

                    "confidence": round(min(0.95, 0.5 + 0.15 * (n - 1)), 2),  # ponytail: evidence-count prior
                    "evidence": r["evidence"][-5:], "first_seen": day(r["first"]), "last_seen": day(r["last"]),
                    "_last": r["last"]})
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["count"], r.pop("_last")), reverse=True)

def collect(project=None):
    """Curated LoRA data: only turns the user accepted, secrets redacted, split by session
    in time order (oldest -> train, newer -> valid, newest -> test) so no session leaks across."""
    from .bench import holdout
    from .memory import _redact
    since = float(open(config.TRACE_MARK, encoding="utf-8").read()) if os.path.exists(config.TRACE_MARK) else 0.0
    pdir = project_dir(project or os.getcwd())
    dirs = [pdir] if os.path.isdir(pdir) else glob.glob(os.path.join(config.PROJECTS, "*"))
    held = holdout()
    sessions, seen, dupes, dropped = [], set(), 0, 0
    for d in dirs:
        for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.jsonl")):
            if os.path.getmtime(f) < since or os.path.basename(f)[:-6] in held:
                continue  # held-out bench sessions never become training data
            msgs = [{**m, "content": _redact(m["content"])} for m in parse_session(f)]
            if len(msgs) < 2:
                continue
            bad, examples = rejected(msgs), []
            # one example per accepted assistant turn, with preceding context under budget
            for i, m in enumerate(msgs):
                if m["role"] != "assistant":
                    continue
                if bad[i]:
                    dropped += 1
                    continue
                ctx, size = [], 0
                for prev in reversed(msgs[:i]):
                    size += len(prev["content"])
                    if size > config.CTX_BUDGET:

                    ctx.insert(0, prev)
                if not ctx or ctx[0]["role"] != "user":

                ex = {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": config.SYSTEM}, *ctx, m]}
                sig = hash(json.dumps(ex["messages"], sort_keys=True))

"""Personal benchmark: how close does model X get to what Claude did, on *your* work?

Answer key = your own Claude Code sessions. A task qualifies when Claude ended
it with a git commit and ran a check (tsc / tests / lint / build) that passed.
Each candidate model gets the same prompt on a clean worktree of the commit
*before* Claude's, then the same check runs.

  footprint bench harvest [n]                      pick + validate held-out tasks (default 20)
  footprint bench run <provider/model>… [--memory on|off|both]
  footprint bench                                  show the latest report
  footprint bench upload                           send scores (numbers only) to your profile

Held-out sessions are excluded from memory and from `collect`, so no model can
copy the answer. Pass = check passes AND the model changed at least one file.
"""
import glob, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time

from . import config, context

HOME = os.path.expanduser("~/.footprint/bench")
TASKS = os.path.join(HOME, "tasks.json")
HOLDOUT = os.path.join(HOME, "holdout.txt")       # session ids kept out of memory + training
RESULTS = os.path.join(HOME, "results.json")
COMMIT = re.compile(r"\[[^\]\s]+(?: \(root-commit\))? ([0-9a-f]{7,40})\]"   # git commit output
                    r"|(?:^|<tool_result>)([0-9a-f]{7,12}) \S", re.M)         # or `git log --oneline` after -q
CHECK = re.compile(r"\b(npx tsc\b.*--noEmit|tsc --noEmit|(?:npm|pnpm|yarn|bun) (?:run )?(?:test|lint|build|typecheck)\b"
                   r"|(?:python3? -m |uvx )?pytest\b|go test\b|cargo (?:test|check|build)\b|next build\b|ruff check\b"
                   r"|node --check\b|(?:npx )?eslint\b|python3? -m (?!pip\b|venv\b|http\b|json\b)[\w.]+\s*$)")
# replaying these would touch the real world (remotes, prod, inboxes): never bench them
SIDE_EFFECT = re.compile(r"\b(push|deploy|publish|release|merge|send|e-?mail|notion|slack|login|vercel|npm i)\b", re.I)
NO_PUSH = {"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT": "3", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0",  # any push in a bench run hits a dead URL
           **{f"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_{i}": "url.blocked-by-footprint-bench://.pushInsteadOf" for i in range(3)},
           "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0": "https://", "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1": "git@", "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2": "ssh://"}
IMAGE = re.compile(r"\.(png|jpe?g|gif|webp)\b", re.I)
ACTIVE_S = 600                                    # sessions touched this recently are live: never hold them out
DEP_DIRS = ("node_modules", ".venv", "venv")      # ponytail: symlinked from the real repo; per-task installs if this proves flaky
RUN_TIMEOUT, CHECK_TIMEOUT = 900, 300


def holdout():
    return set(open(HOLDOUT).read().split()) if os.path.exists(HOLDOUT) else set()


def _git(cwd, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cwd, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def _check_cmd(command, cwd, root):
    """Pull the check segment out of a chained Claude command -> (subdir relative to repo root, cmd)."""
    here = cwd
    for seg in re.split(r"&&|;|\|\|", command):
        seg = seg.split("|")[0].replace("2>&1", "").strip()
        if seg.startswith("cd "):
            here = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(here, os.path.expanduser(seg[3:].strip().strip("'\""))))
        elif CHECK.search(seg):
            rel = os.path.relpath(here, root)
            return (None if rel.startswith("..") else rel), seg
    return None, None

**Commits:** `4248cdc` and `0874792` are on `feat/memory-layers`, not pushed, and not in `main` yet.

**What this round built:**
- **Your own code as training data.** These are commits by you, with no AI edit to their files in the 2 days before and no Claude co-author line. `collect` now turns them into training examples: 7 on this machine.
  - My first version wrongly counted commits I made in this session as yours, and counted worktree commits twice. Both are fixed.
- **Bench went from 1 task to 10.**
  - Tasks where the commit happened in a later turn ("yes commit") are now found through git.
  - Tasks that never ran a check use the repo's own check (typecheck, `tsc`, `pytest`).
  - The 10 tasks come from footprint, Pi-Commerce and Paytmcall, and each one's check passes at the commit.

- **30+ bench tasks.** Your Claude history only has about 10 tasks that end in a commit with a passing check. OpenCode sessions aren't harvested yet, which is the next source. The 10 tasks' sessions (6 in total) are now kept out of memory and training so no model can copy the answer.

- **Same-wording rival tools.** "Use pnpm" vs "use npm" still isn't caught as a contradiction.

Should I push to `main`, and which model should the bench run with?

def _resolve(out):
    """Tasks committed in a later turn get their commit via git; drop ones a replay can't use."""
    for t in out:  # committed in a later turn ("yes commit")? find it via git: first commit touching its files
        if not t["commit"] and t["files"] and t["t"] and t["cwd"] and os.path.isdir(t["cwd"]):
            hit = _git(t["cwd"], "log", f"--since=@{int(t['t'])}", f"--until=@{int(t['t']) + 172800}", "--reverse",
                       "--format=%h", "--", *t["files"]).stdout.split()
            t["commit"] = hit[0] if hit else None
    return [t for t in out if t["commit"] and t["cwd"]
            and not IMAGE.search(t["prompt"])  # a replayed model can't see the screenshot
            and not SIDE_EFFECT.search(t["prompt"])]
    from datetime import datetime
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(rec["timestamp"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
    except (KeyError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        return None


def _default_check(cwd, root):
    """No check in the session? Use the repo's own: typecheck script, tsc, pytest. -> (subdir, cmd) or (None, None)"""
    for d in dict.fromkeys([cwd, root]):  # task folder first, then repo root
        rel = os.path.relpath(d, root)
        try:
            scripts = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, "package.json"))).get("scripts") or {}
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            scripts = {}
        if "typecheck" in scripts:
            return rel, "npm run typecheck"
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "tsconfig.json")):
            return rel, "npx tsc --noEmit"
        if any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, f)) for f in ("pytest.ini", "conftest.py")) \
                or "[tool.pytest" in (open(os.path.join(d, "pyproject.toml")).read() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "pyproject.toml")) else ""):
            return rel, "python3 -m pytest -q"
    return None, None


def _worktree(root, rev):
    """Isolated copy at `rev`: own .git (a worktree would write a model's commits/branches into the
    real repo's .git) and no remote, so nothing a model does can reach the real repo."""
    wt = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fp-bench-")
    ok = subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", "--shared", "--no-checkout", root, wt], capture_output=True).returncode == 0 \
        and _git(wt, "checkout", "-q", "--detach", rev).returncode == 0
    if not ok:
        shutil.rmtree(wt, ignore_errors=True)
        return None
    _git(wt, "remote", "remove", "origin")
    for d in DEP_DIRS:  # deps aren't in git; borrow the real repo's
        for src in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, d)) + glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*", d)):
            dst = os.path.join(wt, os.path.relpath(src, root))
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.dirname(dst)) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                os.symlink(src, dst)
    return wt


def _drop(root, wt):
    shutil.rmtree(wt, ignore_errors=True)


def _run_check(wt, task):
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(task["check_cmd"], shell=True, cwd=os.path.join(wt, task["check_dir"]),
                           capture_output=True, timeout=CHECK_TIMEOUT)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return False


def harvest(argv=()):
    """Newest qualifying tasks whose check really passes at Claude's commit -> held-out set."""
    n = int(argv[0]) if argv and argv[0].isdigit() else 20
    found, seen = [], set()
    from .memory import ARCHIVE
    live = glob.glob(os.path.join(config.PROJECTS, "*", "*.jsonl"))
    names = {os.path.basename(f) for f in live}  # plus archived copies of sessions Claude Code deleted
    files = sorted(live + [a for a in glob.glob(os.path.join(ARCHIVE, "*", "*.jsonl")) if os.path.basename(a) not in names],
                   key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True)
    for f in files:
        if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(f) < ACTIVE_S:
            continue
        for t in _tasks_in(f):
            root = _git(t["cwd"], "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").stdout.strip() if os.path.isdir(t["cwd"]) else ""
            if not root or t["commit"] in seen:
                continue
            parent = _git(root, "rev-parse", f"{t['commit']}^").stdout.strip()
            t["check_dir"], t["check_cmd"] = _check_cmd(t["check"], t["cwd"], root) if t["check"] else (None, None)
            if not t["check_cmd"]:
                t["check_dir"], t["check_cmd"] = _default_check(t["cwd"], root)
            if not parent or not t["check_cmd"]:
                continue
            t.update(root=root, parent=parent,
                     claude_files=_git(root, "diff", "--name-only", parent, t["commit"]).stdout.split())
            wt = _worktree(root, t["commit"])
            ok = wt and _run_check(wt, t)
            if wt:
                _drop(root, wt)
            if ok and t["claude_files"]:
                seen.add(t["commit"])
                found.append(t)
                print(f"  ✓ {os.path.basename(root)} {t['commit'][:7]}  {t['prompt'][:70]!r}")
            if len(found) >= n:
                break
        if len(found) >= n:
            break
    os.makedirs(HOME, exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(found, open(TASKS, "w"), indent=1)
    open(HOLDOUT, "w").write("\n".join(sorted({t["sid"] for t in found})) + "\n")

def _resolve(out):
    """Tasks committed in a later turn get their commit via git; drop ones a replay can't use."""
    for t in out:  # committed in a later turn ("yes commit")? find it via git: first commit touching its files
        if not t["commit"] and t["files"] and t["t"] and t["cwd"] and os.path.isdir(t["cwd"]):

                       "--format=%h", "--", *t["files"]).stdout.split()

def _default_check(cwd, root):
    """No check in the session? Use the repo's own: typecheck script, tsc, pytest. -> (subdir, cmd) or (None, None)"""
    for d in dict.fromkeys([cwd, root]):  # task folder first, then repo root
        rel = os.path.relpath(d, root)
        try:
            scripts = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, "package.json"))).get("scripts") or {}
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            scripts = {}
        if "typecheck" in scripts:
            return rel, "npm run typecheck"
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "tsconfig.json")):
            return rel, "npx tsc --noEmit"
        if any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, f)) for f in ("pytest.ini", "conftest.py")) \
                or "[tool.pytest" in (open(os.path.join(d, "pyproject.toml")).read() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "pyproject.toml")) else ""):
            return rel, "python3 -m pytest -q"
    return None, None


def _worktree(root, rev):
    """Isolated copy at `rev`: own .git (a worktree would write a model's commits/branches into the
    real repo's .git) and no remote, so nothing a model does can reach the real repo."""
    wt = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fp-bench-")
    ok = subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", "--shared", "--no-checkout", root, wt], capture_output=True).returncode == 0 \
        and _git(wt, "checkout", "-q", "--detach", rev).returncode == 0
    if not ok:
        shutil.rmtree(wt, ignore_errors=True)
        return None
    _git(wt, "remote", "remove", "origin")
    for d in DEP_DIRS:  # deps aren't in git; borrow the real repo's
        for src in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, d)) + glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*", d)):
            dst = os.path.join(wt, os.path.relpath(src, root))
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.dirname(dst)) and not os.path.exists(dst):
                os.symlink(src, dst)
    return wt


def _drop(root, wt):
    shutil.rmtree(wt, ignore_errors=True)

"""Parse Claude Code transcripts into training examples."""
import glob, json, os, random, re, subprocess, sys

from . import config


def _text(content, cap=None):
    """Flatten a Claude message content (str or block list) to training text."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        out = content
    else:
        parts = []
        for b in content or []:
            t = b.get("type")
            if t == "text":
                parts.append(b["text"])
            elif t == "tool_use":
                parts.append(f'<tool name="{b["name"]}">{json.dumps(b.get("input", {}))}</tool>')
            elif t == "tool_result":
                c = b.get("content")
                c = "".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c) if isinstance(c, list) else str(c or "")
                parts.append(f"<tool_result>{c[:config.RESULT_CAP]}</tool_result>")
        out = "\n".join(p for p in parts if p.strip())
    out = re.sub(r"<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>", "", out, flags=re.S)
    out = re.sub(r"<local-command-caveat>.*?</local-command-caveat>", "", out, flags=re.S)
    return (out[:cap] if cap else out).strip()


def parse_session(path):
    """One transcript file -> list of alternating {role, content} messages."""
    msgs = []
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") not in ("user", "assistant") or rec.get("isSidechain") or rec.get("isMeta"):
            continue
        m = rec.get("message") or {}
        role = m.get("role")
        txt = _text(m.get("content"))
        if not role or not txt:
            continue
        if msgs and msgs[-1]["role"] == role:
            msgs[-1]["content"] += "\n" + txt
        else:
            msgs.append({"role": role, "content": txt})
    return msgs


def project_dir(path):
    """~/.claude/projects/<slug> for a working dir. Claude Code maps every non-alphanumeric char to '-'."""
    return os.path.join(config.PROJECTS, re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", os.path.abspath(path)))


def rejected(msgs):
    """Per message: True if it belongs to a task the user pushed back on — their next real
    prompt is a correction ("no, …", "still broken") or they interrupted it mid-way."""
    from .memory import is_correction
    prompts = [i for i, m in enumerate(msgs) if m["role"] == "user" and not m["content"].startswith("<tool_result>")]

ITERS_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_ITERS_CAP", "2000"))  # ceiling so big datasets stay tractable

CTX_BUDGET = 6000      # chars of history per training example

CONTEXT_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_CAP", "4000"))  # chars injected at session start (~1k tokens)
CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H = float(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H", "168"))  # older previous session = stale, skip
MEMORY_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_MEMORY_CAP", "1500"))  # chars of similar past work injected per prompt
PROFILE_CAP = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_PROFILE_CAP", "1500"))  # chars of profile + project memory at session start
EMBED_MODEL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_EMBED_MODEL", "nomic-embed-text")  # Ollama; absent = BM25-only recall
OLLAMA_URL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434")

def has_adapter():
    return any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(ADAPTERS, f))
               for f in ("adapters.safetensors", "adapter_model.safetensors"))


def ensure_test():
    """Path to the held-out test set (newest sessions, written by collect, never trained or validated on)."""
    test = os.path.join(DATA, "test.jsonl")
    if not os.path.exists(test):
        sys.exit("no test data. run: footprint collect")
    return test


def resolve_iters():
    """Training steps. FOOTPRINT_ITERS overrides; else EPOCHS passes over the
    train set (batch-1 => 1 step/example), clamped to [100, ITERS_CAP].
    Fixed 300 iters saw <1 epoch of a few-thousand-example set — this scales."""
    if ITERS:
        return str(ITERS)
    tr = os.path.join(DATA, "train.jsonl")
    n = sum(1 for _ in open(tr)) if os.path.exists(tr) else 0
    return str(max(100, min(ITERS_CAP, math.ceil(EPOCHS * n / max(BATCH, 1)))))


if __name__ == "__main__":  # sanity: ITERS override + clamp/epoch math
    globals()["ITERS"] = "42"; assert resolve_iters() == "42"
    _f = lambda n: max(100, min(2000, math.ceil(3.0 * n / 1)))
    assert _f(5713) == 2000   # big set hits cap
    assert _f(200) == 600     # mid set = 3 epochs
    assert _f(5) == 100       # tiny set floored
    print("resolve_iters clamp/epoch math ok")

SYSTEM = ("You are footprint, a local coding agent trained on Claude Code sessions. "
          "To act, emit tool calls as <tool name=\"NAME\">{json args}</tool>. "
          "Say DONE when the task is complete.")


def has_adapter():
    return any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(ADAPTERS, f))
               for f in ("adapters.safetensors", "adapter_model.safetensors"))


def ensure_test():
    """Path to the held-out test set (newest sessions, written by collect, never trained or validated on)."""
    test = os.path.join(DATA, "test.jsonl")
    if not os.path.exists(test):
        sys.exit("no test data. run: footprint collect")
    return test


def resolve_iters():
    """Training steps. FOOTPRINT_ITERS overrides; else EPOCHS passes over the
    train set (batch-1 => 1 step/example), clamped to [100, ITERS_CAP].
    Fixed 300 iters saw <1 epoch of a few-thousand-example set — this scales."""
    if ITERS:
        return str(ITERS)
    tr = os.path.join(DATA, "train.jsonl")
    n = sum(1 for _ in open(tr)) if os.path.exists(tr) else 0
    return str(max(100, min(ITERS_CAP, math.ceil(EPOCHS * n / max(BATCH, 1)))))

    globals()["ITERS"] = "42"; assert resolve_iters() == "42"
    _f = lambda n: max(100, min(2000, math.ceil(3.0 * n / 1)))
    assert _f(5713) == 2000   # big set hits cap
    assert _f(200) == 600     # mid set = 3 epochs
    assert _f(5) == 100       # tiny set floored
    print("resolve_iters clamp/epoch math ok")

"""Linux/Windows backend: transformers + peft (CUDA if available, else CPU)."""
import json, os

from .. import config


def train():
    from datasets import load_dataset
    from peft import LoraConfig
    from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer
    ds = load_dataset("json", data_files={"train": os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl"),
                                          "valid": os.path.join(config.DATA, "valid.jsonl")})
    trainer = SFTTrainer(
        model=config.MODEL,
        args=SFTConfig(output_dir=config.ADAPTERS, max_steps=int(config.resolve_iters()),
                       per_device_train_batch_size=config.BATCH, gradient_checkpointing=True,
                       max_length=4096, logging_steps=25, report_to=[]),
        train_dataset=ds["train"], eval_dataset=ds["valid"],
        peft_config=LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules="all-linear"))
    trainer.train()
    trainer.save_model(config.ADAPTERS)
    print(f"adapter saved -> {config.ADAPTERS}")


def evaluate():
    import math
    from datasets import load_dataset
    from peft import PeftModel
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
    from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer
    if not config.has_adapter():
        raise SystemExit("no trained adapter. run: footprint train")
    ds = load_dataset("json", data_files={"test": config.ensure_test()})
    base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(config.MODEL, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto")
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, config.ADAPTERS)
    trainer = SFTTrainer(model=model, eval_dataset=ds["test"],
                         args=SFTConfig(output_dir=config.ADAPTERS, max_length=4096,
                                        per_device_eval_batch_size=config.BATCH, report_to=[]))
    loss = trainer.evaluate()["eval_loss"]
    print(f"Test loss {loss:.3f}, Test ppl {math.exp(loss):.3f}")


def serve():
    import torch
    from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(config.MODEL)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(config.MODEL, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto")
    if config.has_adapter():
        from peft import PeftModel
        model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, config.ADAPTERS)
    else:
        print("(no adapter yet — serving base model; run train first for footprint behavior)")
    model.eval()

    def generate(messages, max_tokens, temperature):
        ids = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                      return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=max_tokens, do_sample=temperature > 0,
                                 temperature=max(temperature, 1e-3),
                                 pad_token_id=tok.eos_token_id)
        return tok.decode(out[0][ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def _json(self, obj, ctype="application/json"):
            body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path.startswith("/v1/models"):
                self._json({"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "footprint", "object": "model"}]})
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

        def do_POST(self):
            if self.path.rstrip("/") != "/v1/chat/completions":
                self.send_error(404)
                return
            req = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
            text = generate(req.get("messages", []), req.get("max_tokens") or 1024,
                            req.get("temperature") if req.get("temperature") is not None else 0.7)
            if req.get("stream"):
                # ponytail: whole answer as one SSE chunk; true token streaming if UX needs it
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()
                for payload in (
                        {"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "model": "footprint",
                         "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                                      "finish_reason": None}]},
                        {"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "model": "footprint",
                         "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}):
                    self.wfile.write(f"data: {json.dumps(payload)}\n\n".encode())
                self.wfile.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
            else:
                self._json({"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "footprint",
                            "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                                         "finish_reason": "stop"}]})

        def log_message(self, *a):
            pass

    print(f"OpenAI-compatible API: http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1  (model name: footprint)\n"
          f"device: {'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'}")
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(config.PORT)), Handler).serve_forever()

`footprint bench run footprint/<model>` is the gate before you keep it.
"""
import glob, hashlib, json, os, shutil, sys, time

from . import config


def versions():
    return sorted((os.path.basename(d) for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "v*"))
                   if os.path.basename(d)[1:].isdigit()), key=lambda v: int(v[1:]))


def metrics(v):
    try:
        return json.load(open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v, "metrics.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def migrate():
    """v1 format (adapters/ root, custom <tool> format) -> adapters/<model>/v1, kept for rollback."""
    old = os.path.join(config.ADAPTER_ROOT, "adapters.safetensors")
    if not os.path.exists(old):
        return
    dst = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "v1")
    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(config.ADAPTER_ROOT, "*.safetensors")) + \
            glob.glob(os.path.join(config.ADAPTER_ROOT, "adapter_config.json")):
        shutil.move(f, os.path.join(dst, os.path.basename(f)))
    json.dump({"version": "v1", "format": "legacy <tool> text", "note": "trained before v2; 100 iters"},
              open(os.path.join(dst, "metrics.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    if not config.active_version():
        use("v1", quiet=True)


def new_version():
    migrate()
    vs = versions()
    v = f"v{int(vs[-1][1:]) + 1 if vs else 1}"
    path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v)
    os.makedirs(path)
    return v, path


def data_hash():
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in ("train", "valid", "test"):
        p = os.path.join(config.DATA, f"{name}.jsonl")
        if os.path.exists(p):
            h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
    return h.hexdigest()[:12]


def finish(v, m):
    """Save metrics; go live only if no adapter is active or this one has a lower test loss."""
    m = {"version": v, "model": config.MODEL, "data": data_hash(), "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), **m}
    json.dump(m, open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v, "metrics.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    cur = config.active_version()
    old = metrics(cur).get("test_loss") if cur else None
    if cur is None or (m.get("test_loss") is not None and (old is None or m["test_loss"] < old)):
        use(v, quiet=True)
        print(f"{v} is now active (test loss {m.get('test_loss')} vs {old if cur else 'none'}). "
              f"Gate it: footprint bench run <footprint model in opencode> --memory=both; rollback: footprint adapter use {cur}"
              if cur else f"{v} is now active.")
    else:
        print(f"{v} saved but NOT active: test loss {m.get('test_loss')} is not better than {cur}'s {old}. "
              f"Use anyway: footprint adapter use {v}")


def use(v, quiet=False):
    if v not in versions():
        sys.exit(f"no {v}. have: {', '.join(versions()) or 'none'}")
    open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "active"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(v)
    if not quiet:
        print(f"active adapter: {v} — restart the server to load it (footprint serve, or re-run footprint install)")


def main(argv=()):
    migrate()
    if argv[:1] == ["use"] and len(argv) > 1:
        return use(argv[1])
    cur = config.active_version()
    print(f"adapters for {config.MODEL}:")
    for v in versions():
        m = metrics(v)
        print(f"  {'*' if v == cur else ' '} {v}  {m.get('format', ''):<22} test loss {m.get('test_loss', '?')}  "
              f"val {m.get('val_loss', '?')}  best iter {m.get('best_iter', '?')}  data {m.get('data', '?')}  {m.get('created', '')}")
    if not versions():
        print("  none yet. run: footprint collect && footprint train")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: versions, gate, migrate, rollback in a temp root
    import tempfile
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    config.ADAPTER_ROOT, config.DATA = d, d
    config.MODEL_ADAPTERS = os.path.join(d, "m")
    open(os.path.join(d, "adapters.safetensors"), "w").write("old")
    v, p = new_version()  # migrates legacy to v1 (active), returns v2
    assert v == "v2" and versions() == ["v1", "v2"] and config.active_version() == "v1", (v, versions())
    finish("v2", {"test_loss": 2.0, "format": "native-v2"})
    assert config.active_version() == "v2"  # legacy had no test loss: v2 wins
    v3, _ = new_version()
    finish(v3, {"test_loss": 2.5})
    assert config.active_version() == "v2"  # worse: saved, not live
    use("v3", quiet=True)
    assert config.active_version() == "v3"
    use("v2", quiet=True)  # rollback
    assert config.active_version() == "v2" and metrics("v3")["test_loss"] == 2.5
    print("adapters self-check ok")

"""Apple Silicon backend: mlx-lm (train + OpenAI-compatible server)."""
import json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys

from .. import adapters, config


def train():
    """LoRA v2: native chat/tool format, loss on the answer only, rank 16 on every layer,
    best checkpoint by validation loss (early stop), new version gated on test loss."""
    iters = int(config.resolve_iters())
    every = max(25, iters // 10)
    v, out = adapters.new_version()
    cfg = os.path.join(out, "train_config.yaml")
    with open(cfg, "w") as f:  # JSON is valid YAML
        json.dump({"lora_parameters": {"rank": config.LORA_RANK, "scale": config.LORA_ALPHA / config.LORA_RANK,
                                       "dropout": 0.05}}, f)
    print(f"training {v}: {iters} iters, rank {config.LORA_RANK}, eval/save every {every} (batch {config.BATCH})")
    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "lora", "--model", config.MODEL, "--train",
                          "--data", config.DATA, "--adapter-path", out, "-c", cfg, "--mask-prompt",
                          "--num-layers", "-1", "--learning-rate", config.LEARNING_RATE,
                          "--iters", str(iters), "--steps-per-eval", str(every), "--save-every", str(every),
                          "--val-batches", "25", "--max-seq-length", "4096",
                          "--batch-size", str(config.BATCH), "--grad-checkpoint"],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
    val = {}
    for line in p.stdout:
        print(line, end="")
        if m := re.search(r"Iter (\d+): Val loss ([\d.]+)", line):
            val[int(m.group(1))] = float(m.group(2))
    if p.wait():
        sys.exit(f"training failed; partial output kept in {out}")
    saved = {it: l for it, l in val.items() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, f"{it:07d}_adapters.safetensors"))}
    best = min(saved, key=saved.get) if saved else None
    if best is not None and best != iters:  # early stop: later iters overfit, keep the best one
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(out, f"{best:07d}_adapters.safetensors"), os.path.join(out, "adapters.safetensors"))
    test = evaluate(out)
    adapters.finish(v, {"format": "native-v2", "iters": iters, "best_iter": best or iters,
                        "val_loss": saved.get(best) if best else None, "test_loss": test,
                        "rank": config.LORA_RANK, "lr": config.LEARNING_RATE})


def evaluate(path=None):
    """Test loss of an adapter on the newest sessions (never trained or validated on). -> float"""
    path = path or config.ADAPTERS
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, "adapters.safetensors")):
        sys.exit("no trained adapter. run: footprint train")
    config.ensure_test()
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "lora", "--model", config.MODEL,
                        "--data", config.DATA, "--adapter-path", path, "--mask-prompt",
                        "--test", "--max-seq-length", "4096", "--test-batches", str(config.TEST_BATCHES),
                        "--batch-size", str(config.BATCH)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(r.stdout[-400:] + r.stderr[-400:] if r.returncode else r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    m = re.search(r"Test loss ([\d.]+)", r.stdout)
    return float(m.group(1)) if m else None


def serve():
    args = [sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "server", "--model", config.MODEL,
            "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", config.PORT]
    if config.has_adapter():
        args += ["--adapter-path", config.ADAPTERS]
        print(f"adapter: {config.active_version()}")
    else:
        print("(no adapter yet — serving base model; run train first for footprint behavior)")
    print(f"OpenAI-compatible API: http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1  (model name: footprint)")
    subprocess.run(args, check=True)

"""Apple Silicon backend: mlx-lm (train + OpenAI-compatible server)."""
import json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys

from .. import adapters, config


def train():
    """LoRA v2: native chat/tool format, loss on the answer only, rank 16 on every layer,
    best checkpoint by validation loss (early stop), new version gated on test loss."""
    iters = int(config.resolve_iters())
    every = max(25, iters // 10)
    v, out = adapters.new_version()
    cfg = os.path.join(out, "train_config.yaml")
    with open(cfg, "w") as f:  # JSON is valid YAML
        json.dump({"lora_parameters": {"rank": config.LORA_RANK, "scale": config.LORA_ALPHA / config.LORA_RANK,
                                       "dropout": 0.05}}, f)
    print(f"training {v}: {iters} iters, rank {config.LORA_RANK}, eval/save every {every} (batch {config.BATCH})")
    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "lora", "--model", config.MODEL, "--train",
                          "--data", config.DATA, "--adapter-path", out, "-c", cfg, "--mask-prompt",
                          "--num-layers", "-1", "--learning-rate", config.LEARNING_RATE,
                          "--iters", str(iters), "--steps-per-eval", str(every), "--save-every", str(every),
                          "--val-batches", "25", "--max-seq-length", "4096",
                          "--batch-size", str(config.BATCH), "--grad-checkpoint"],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
    val = {}
    for line in p.stdout:
        print(line, end="")
        if m := re.search(r"Iter (\d+): Val loss ([\d.]+)", line):
            val[int(m.group(1))] = float(m.group(2))
    if p.wait():
        sys.exit(f"training failed; partial output kept in {out}")
    saved = {it: l for it, l in val.items() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, f"{it:07d}_adapters.safetensors"))}
    best = min(saved, key=saved.get) if saved else None
    if best is not None and best != iters:  # early stop: later iters overfit, keep the best one
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(out, f"{best:07d}_adapters.safetensors"), os.path.join(out, "adapters.safetensors"))
    test = evaluate(out)
    adapters.finish(v, {"format": "native-v2", "iters": iters, "best_iter": best or iters,
                        "val_loss": saved.get(best) if best else None, "test_loss": test,
                        "rank": config.LORA_RANK, "lr": config.LEARNING_RATE})


def evaluate(path=None):
    """Test loss of an adapter on the newest sessions (never trained or validated on). -> float"""
    path = path or config.ADAPTERS
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, "adapters.safetensors")):
        sys.exit("no trained adapter. run: footprint train")
    config.ensure_test()
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "lora", "--model", config.MODEL,
                        "--data", config.DATA, "--adapter-path", path, "--mask-prompt",
                        "--test", "--max-seq-length", "4096", "--test-batches", str(config.TEST_BATCHES),
                        "--batch-size", str(config.BATCH)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(r.stdout[-400:] + r.stderr[-400:] if r.returncode else r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    m = re.search(r"Test loss ([\d.]+)", r.stdout)
    return float(m.group(1)) if m else None


def serve():
    args = [sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "server", "--model", config.MODEL,
            "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", config.PORT]
    if config.has_adapter():
        args += ["--adapter-path", config.ADAPTERS]
        print(f"adapter: {config.active_version()}")
    else:
        print("(no adapter yet — serving base model; run train first for footprint behavior)")
    print(f"OpenAI-compatible API: http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1  (model name: footprint)")
    subprocess.run(args, check=True)
EOF

Both jobs lost the night to the laptop sleeping:

- **Bench (memory on vs off):** 8 of 60 replays done in 13.5 hours; it was suspended while the laptop slept. It's moving again now, and the rest will take hours with the laptop awake.
- **Smoke training:** the model weights had never been downloaded, so the run was stuck on the download, which stalled when the network dropped during sleep. I fixed it: training now runs offline only when the weights are present, and shows progress live. The weights (0.9 GB) are downloaded and the smoke test is running again. It's slow: about 10 minutes without reaching step 25, with swap nearly full on 8 GB.

I'll start the real training once the smoke test finishes, and only if it works. If 50 steps take 20+ minutes, the full run of about 840 steps would take around 6 hours. In that case I'll suggest smaller settings (shorter sequences or fewer layers) before starting it.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

attachment.content:
- footprint: Local SLM that learns from Claude Code transcripts ("footprint") and replays the project's working style. Trigger on /footprint, "take footprint", "train footprint", "footprint status", "footprint run <task>".

PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.
